text:
Many Indian cities still carry a planning decision made 160 years ago.
Colonial cities were laid out as three towns: the old city, the military cantonment, and Civil Lines for the senior civil officers, kept apart from both.
The building block was the bungalow compound: one house on a large walled plot along wide, tree-lined roads. In Allahabad (Prayagraj) the Civil Lines was laid out in 1858 on eight villages; in Delhi it housed the administration until New Delhi.
Britannica still describes these areas by their openness, trees and older one-storey bungalows. Prayagraj's Civil Lines, by contrast, is now a business district with high-rises.
